title: Cloud account takeover: MFA-fatigue -> impossible travel -> OAuth persistence

anomaly.summary: Anomaly trigger: a burst of denied MFA push challenges followed by a successful SSO login for the same user
anomaly.spl: index=saas sourcetype=okta:authentication result=MFA_DENIED | stats count by user,src_ip

decoy_hypothesis.statement: H1: User {bf_ip} logged in from two countries minutes apart — that is the impossible-travel account takeover.
decoy_hypothesis.seed_spl: index=saas sourcetype=okta:authentication action=success user=s.muller | stats dc(geo_country) as count by user | rename user as src_ip

refutation.success_check_spl: index=saas sourcetype=okta:authentication action=success user=s.muller | lookup threat_intel.csv indicator as src_ip OUTPUT verdict | where verdict!="benign"
refutation.no_success_reason: every source IP for s.muller is sanctioned corporate VPN egress (US and EU egress of the same VPN), not attacker infrastructure
refutation.benign_reason: threat intel rates those egress IPs benign ({ti_note})

corrected_hypothesis.statement: H2: The real account takeover is d.okafor: after an MFA-fatigue push-bombing burst from a malicious residential proxy in Lagos (102.89.40.7), the attacker authenticated, consented a malicious OAuth app (MailRuleSyncer) with mail.send + offline_access for persistence, created an inbox-hiding rule, and pulled a finance board deck — s.muller's US/EU VPN hops are sanctioned, not travel.
corroborating_spl: index=saas sourcetype=okta:authentication action=success user=d.okafor | table user,geo_country,src_ip
corrected_hypothesis.rationale: SPL shows d.okafor's success from a malicious-rated Lagos proxy plus a malicious OAuth grant and an inbox rule — a corroborated takeover chain, while s.muller's geo change is benign VPN egress.

root_cause: An attacker used MFA push-fatigue from a malicious residential proxy to take over d.okafor's SSO account, then consented a malicious OAuth application (MailRuleSyncer) with mail and offline_access scopes to establish token persistence and created a mailbox rule to hide its activity.

blast_radius.identity_query: index=saas sourcetype=okta:system event=app.oauth2.client.consent.grant | dedup user | table user

remediation: Force a password reset AND revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for d.okafor.
Revoke the MailRuleSyncer OAuth grant and block the app tenant-wide; require admin approval for third-party apps.
Delete the malicious inbox rule and review for further mailbox manipulation / forwarding.
Block the malicious proxy 102.89.40.7 and add a detection for MFA-denied bursts preceding a success.
Switch the affected group from push to number-matching or FIDO2 MFA to defeat push fatigue.
Notify d.okafor and audit what the finance board deck exposure requires.
